question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 19 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The flash sale campaign likely caused the sudden increase in request volume and error rate.
why_chain: The flash sale campaign went live at the right time and place (127 minutes before the change).
This led to a significant increase in request volume and error rate.
The sudden increase in traffic overwhelmed the system, causing the p95 latency to rise.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The deployment of auth v4.9 to ap-south caused the increase in latency.
ruled_out.reason: The deployment happened hours before the change, not at the right time and place.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The deployment of catalog v1.1 to us-east caused the increase in latency.
ruled_out.reason: The deployment happened hours before the change, not at the right time and place.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The deployment of catalog v1.1 to us-east caused the scaling out in ap-south.
ruled_out.reason: The deployment happened hours before the change, not at the right time and place.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The deployment of catalog v1.1 to us-east may have caused the scaling out in ap-south.
ruled_out.reason: It rests on a change that is too early, or in a different service/region, to explain a sudden change here.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The deployment of auth v4.9 to ap-south may have caused the increase in latency.
ruled_out.reason: It rests on a change that is too early, or in a different service/region, to explain a sudden change here.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for region ap-south rose from 137 ms to 284 ms (+107%), with a change point at 2026-03-19T03:30:00Z.
The change is concentrated in region ap-south: 4 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.01).
At the same time, request volume for region ap-south rose (1267 per 5 min before, 4623 per 5 min after, +265%).
At the same time, error rate for region ap-south rose (0.41% before, 0.81% after, +100%).
Marketing: flash sale campaign goes live in ap-south at 03:30 UTC (ap-south; 127 min before the change; record R015; fit: right time and place: a strong candidate cause)
Request volume 3x normal in ap-south (ap-south; 12 min after the change; record R016; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
Deployed auth v4.9 to ap-south (auth, ap-south; 251 min before the change; record R013; fit: hours before the change, too early to explain a sudden jump)
autoscaler: scaling out, 4 new instances requested (ap-south; 20 min after the change; record R017; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
Deployed catalog v1.1 to us-east (routine release) (catalog, us-east; 163 min before the change; record R014; fit: different service/region, so unlikely to be the cause)

reasons: ✓ A change event (tickets) lines up in time (127 min before the change).
✓ 2 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume rose, as a traffic cause requires.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.

actions.action: Roll back the deployment of auth v4.9 to ap-south
Monitor the impact of the flash sale campaign and adjust resources accordingly
